title: add representative workload runners and reporting pipeline for benchmark lab
author: Aisha Raman
description: Context: The benchmark lab needs a compact set of representative workload runners and a reporting pipeline that can ingest profiling baselines (latency/throughput/cost) and produce daily summaries for dashboards and regression detection. This PR adds: 1) representative workload runners (chat generation, streaming responses, embeddings batching, long-context decoding) with config-driven parameters and sample workload YAMLs; 2) a baseline collector that runs canonical workloads to produce profiling baselines (p95/p50 latencies, token throughput, memory footprint) and stores artifacts; 3) a reporting pipeline ingestion stage that normalizes metrics, annotates by model variant/hardware, and writes aggregated rows to BigQuery/GCS; 4) CI integration (nightly and on-demand) and documentation. The description below lists changes, testing notes and a short migration/usage guide. Checklist: - [x] Add runner skeletons + example configs - [x] Baseline collector and schema v1 - [x] Reporting ingestion/aggregation + failure handling - [x] CI job for nightly runs - [x] Docs and README with runbook Motivation: reduce manual benchmarking overhead, ensure representative coverage across common request patterns, and provide a stable baseline for perf/regression alerts. How to run locally: python benchmark-lab/runners/rep_runner.py --config configs/rep_workloads/chat_small.yaml --output ./out Example CI usage: .github/workflows/nightly-bench.yml triggers on schedule and writes artifacts to gs://redwood-bench/rep/ Date constraints: baseline collector writes dataset with schema_version=1. Notes: this is additive and non-breaking; config-driven design allows adding more workloads without code changes.
